The optimizer reported that its stopping rule was reached. Recorded iterations: 36. Optimizer termination alone does not establish stationarity, numerical accuracy, or valid inference.

Recorded estimation settings were optimizer = EM with analytical-gradient L-BFGS-B M-step; MML engine = em; maximum iterations = 400; stopping tolerance = 1e-12. Facet coefficients in the response predictor were WorkYear: +1, RaterYear: -1, Mode: -1; a positive coefficient increases the expected score as that measure increases. Sum-to-zero constraints were applied to WorkYear, Mode. The selected non-centered facet was RaterYear. The recorded MML quadrature size was 61 nodes. The person population SD was fixed at 1.0.

Run qualification: state=disconnected_mml_cohorts; SupportsFormalInference=FALSE; formal_hold_reason=stat.mml.population_assumption_linked; screening_block_reason=none.

Rating cohorts are disconnected across unanchored facets; cross-cohort MML scale alignment relies solely on the assumed common person distribution rather than shared observations or anchors.

Eligibility of specified intervals does not establish eligibility of person scores or general tables. Automatic equivalence conclusions remain withheld.

Estimates and interval bounds are in logits. SE = standard error; SD = standard deviation; RealSE = ModelSE * sqrt(max(Infit, 1)). Displayed general-table SEs and intervals are exploratory (Use = screening_only; SupportsFormalInference = FALSE). Infit and Outfit are mean-square fit statistics (MnSq), with model expectation 1. Underfit (>1) means more unexplained variation than expected; overfit (<1) means less. These are not ability or rater-quality scores. The review flags use separate thresholds; do not exclude a person or rater on this statistic alone. These are not automatic pass/fail judgments. Levels with ObservedCategories = 1 used only a single score category (zero raw score variance). Posterior SD: conditional posterior spread given fitted parameters, not the sampling SE of EAP; normal bands are screening_only (SupportsFormalInference=FALSE). Withheld: interpretation is on hold; estimates are technical terminal-point values. SE/SD and interval cells are blank. Hold cause: rank-deficient or regularized MML covariance (stat.stat_003.covariance_rank_deficient). Hold cause: Rating cohorts are disconnected across unanchored facets; cross-cohort MML scale alignment relies solely on the assumed common person distribution rather than shared observations or anchors. (stat.mml.population_assumption_linked) Method details and source values are retained in this project.

Categories use the analyzed score coding. Count is the unweighted number of retained ratings; Percent uses all retained ratings as its denominator. Counts alone do not establish category functioning or justify merging categories. All recorded score categories are listed, including zero-count categories when present.

Centered adjacent-category step threshold offsets in logits (sum to zero within common rating scale (StepFacet = Common)). Displayed SEs and 95% normal bands use MML full observed-information delta-method SEs (including the sum-to-zero final step) and are exploratory (SEUse = screening_only; SupportsFormalInference = FALSE). Disordered = True indicates a narrower intermediate modal zone (Spacing < 0), not an automatic category-collapsing rule.

Four descriptive precision series per facet: SEMode = model (ModelSE) vs fit_adjusted (RealSE = ModelSE * sqrt(max(Infit, 1))) crossed with DistributionBasis = sample (ddof=1) vs population (ddof=0). All derived separation/reliability indices are exploratory summaries (Use = screening_only; SupportsFormalInference = FALSE) and do not propagate inter-estimate covariance. EstimateAvailable, SEAvailable, ExcludedLevels and AggregationTarget state the exact calculation scope; JMLE extreme-score boundary persons without finite estimates are excluded explicitly rather than silently dropped. Precision cells (RMSE, TrueSD, Separation, Strata, Reliability) are blank where Use = withheld; inspect StatusReason for the exact cause. Strata (H) = (4G+1)/3 is a conceptual index of distinguishable levels, derived from separation G, not an observed group count or a grouping rule. H = 3 does not establish three actual groups or their cut scores. Reliability here concerns differentiation, not inter-rater agreement; low rater separation can also reflect imprecision. For MML EAP person estimates, Separation = SD(EAP) / RMSE and Reliability = Var(EAP) / (Var(EAP) + RMSE^2); conditional posterior SD is not the sampling SE of EAP. Full notes and original technical values are retained in this project.

FairM and FairZ are model-expected ratings in the original score units, not logits or evidence of fairness. FairM holds other facet locations at their unweighted fitted means (including the person mean for nonperson targets); FairZ holds other locations at zero. These are predictions at reference locations, not averages of predictions. PCM uses the target step-owner's thresholds, or mean thresholds for other targets. An unbounded person mean makes nonperson FairM unavailable; FairZ remains a distinct zero-reference quantity. Boundary and calibration holds are retained. No fair-score SE or interval is implemented; logit SEs cannot be reused.

Wright map

Read the ordering and spacing of person locations (left) and facet locations (right) on the shared logit axis. Under the usual coding, higher locations mean higher person measures, greater rater severity or greater task difficulty. Facet origins depend on identification constraints. Overlap alone does not establish targeting, floor/ceiling effects or validity; inspect score distributions, category boundaries and qualified precision estimates together. After reading locations, use the Pathway map to inspect fit (Boone, 2008). Boone (2008), Teaching students about Rasch maps: https://www.rasch.org/rmt/rmt222a.htm

Pathway map

The vertical axis shows measures; the horizontal axis shows the selected fit statistic. Point size does not encode uncertainty. Infit MnSq (default): compare response variation with the model reference of 1. Larger values indicate more variation, smaller values less. No fixed acceptance band is imposed. Approximate Infit ZSTD uses 0 and reference lines at ±2; counts, degrees of freedom, estimation and multiple comparisons affect interpretation. The figure note identifies the transformation and any cap. Inspect MnSq, counts and the original ratings and content together. MnSq and ZSTD are not universally calibrated tests. Interpretation must account for the data and estimation method (Müller, 2020). Müller (2020), Item fit statistics for Rasch analysis: can we trust them?: https://doi.org/10.1186/s40488-020-00108-7

Category probabilities

The horizontal axis is the person location adjusted for rater, task and other facet effects; the vertical axis is category probability. Inspect whether intermediate categories become most probable alongside observed frequencies, threshold order and rubric meaning. An absent peak alone does not establish category misuse or justify collapsing categories (Linacre, 2002b). Linacre (2002), Optimizing rating scale category effectiveness: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11997586/

Facet-level estimates

Ranked facet-level locations (logits). Displayed interval bars are exploratory screening bands (screening_only; SupportsFormalInference=FALSE); fixed, extreme-score and unidentifiable levels show point locations only.

Step threshold ladder

Centered step threshold ladder (logits). Disordered crossings indicate narrow intermediate modal zones, not an automatic category-collapsing rule.

Diagnostic bubble chart

Diagnostic bubble chart of measure (logits) vs fit statistic, with bubble area proportional to screening ModelSE (or observation count when SE is withheld). Reference lines at 0.5/1.5 (or ±2 ZSTD) are inspection prompts, not fixed cutoffs.

Expected score curve

Expected score curve E[X | eta] across the net logit predictor, bounded by rubric minimum, midpoint and maximum reference lines.

Information and conditional SE

Single-observation category Fisher information I(eta) and conditional SE = 1/sqrt(I(eta)), holding calibration parameters fixed (screening_only; SupportsFormalInference=FALSE).

Fair vs observed average

Fair average (FairM / FairZ) versus observed average score across facet levels. Vertical offsets from the 45-degree identity line show context adjustment for partner-facet locations.

Unexpected responses

Observations with the largest standardized residuals (StdResidual). Reference lines at ±2 and ±3 guide data and rubric inspection rather than automatic deletion.

Standardized residual Q-Q

Normal Q-Q plot of person-aggregated standardized residuals (sum(z)/sqrt(n)), excluding JMLE extreme-score boundary persons. Discrete ratings produce approximate normality only.
